message.content: In Christian theology, **Jesus Christ** is regarded as the most important prophet. While the Old Testament contains many revered prophets—Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and others—Christ is seen as the fulfillment of all prophetic tradition. He is described in the New Testament as the “prophet” who brings the final revelation of God’s will, the one who fulfills the Messianic prophecies of the Hebrew Scriptures, and the one who inaugurates the new covenant. Thus, within Christianity, Jesus is considered the supreme prophet, the ultimate messenger of God.

He is also considered a prophet in some contexts, but the most important prophet might be considered Moses or Isaiah?
